questions.prompt: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.explain: Type 0 (general truth): if + present simple, present simple.

questions.prompt: If the ball crosses the line, it ___ a goal.
questions.explain: Type 0 (rule): if + present simple, present simple.

questions.prompt: When the temperature drops below zero, puddles ___.
questions.explain: Type 0 (general truth): when + present simple, present simple.

questions.prompt: If a player gets two yellow cards, the referee ___ him off.
questions.explain: Type 0 (rule): both clauses are in the present simple; the referee takes -s.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If you mix blue and yellow, you always ___ (to get) green.
questions.explain: Type 0: a general truth uses the present simple in both clauses.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If it ___ (to rain), the grass gets wet.
questions.explain: Type 0: present simple in both clauses; it takes -s.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about a machine is correct?
choices: If you will press the button, the light comes on.
If you pressed the button, the light comes on.
If you press the button, the light comes on.
If you press the button, the light would come on.
questions.answer: If you press the button, the light comes on.
questions.explain: A general truth: present simple in both clauses.

questions.prompt: If a warrior is brave, people ___ him.
questions.explain: Type 0: present simple in both clauses; 'people' is plural, so no -s.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If you ___ (not / to water) a plant, it dies.
questions.explain: Type 0: negative present simple with you: don't + base verb.

questions.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
questions.explain: Type 1: if + present simple, will + base verb; never will after if.

questions.prompt: If I ___ my homework, I will watch TV.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: We will win the match if we ___ hard.
questions.explain: Type 1: no will in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: If Grendel attacks tonight, Beowulf ___ ready.
questions.explain: Type 1: if + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about the weather and a match is correct?
choices: If it will rain, we will cancel the game.
If it rains, we will cancel the game.
If it rained, we will cancel the game.
If it would rain, we will cancel the game.
questions.answer: If it rains, we will cancel the game.
questions.explain: After if, use the present simple, not will.

questions.prompt: If you ___ the bus, you will be late.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: She ___ a new bike if she saves her pocket money.
questions.explain: Type 1 main clause: will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about pocket money is correct?
choices: If I will save £5 a week, I will have enough in a month.
If I would save £5 a week, I will have enough in a month.
If I saved £5 a week, I will have enough in a month.
If I save £5 a week, I will have enough in a month.
questions.answer: If I save £5 a week, I will have enough in a month.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple in the if-clause, will in the main clause.

questions.prompt: When the if-clause comes first, what goes after it? 'If it rains ___ we will stay in.'
questions.explain: An if-clause at the start is followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means the same as 'If you train hard, you will improve.'?
choices: You will improve if you will train hard.
You will improve if you train hard.
You will improve if you trained hard.
You would improve if you train hard.
questions.answer: You will improve if you train hard.
questions.explain: The two clauses can swap places; there is no comma when the if-clause comes second.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If it ___ (to snow) tomorrow, we will build a snowman.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if; it takes -s.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (to see) Anna, I will give her the book.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: We will be late if we ___ (not / to hurry).
questions.explain: Negative present simple with we: don't + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If she ___ (to pass) the test, her parents will be proud.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if; she takes -es.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If the striker ___ (to score) on Sunday, we will win the cup.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if; the striker takes -s.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (to have) time, I will call you.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If Beowulf ___ (to enter) the hall, the warriors will cheer.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if; Beowulf takes -s.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If the weather is bad tomorrow, we ___ (to stay) at home.
questions.explain: Type 1 main clause: will + base verb.

questions.prompt: 'If I find your keys, I will tell you.' What does this show?
questions.explain: Type 1 talks about a possible situation in the future.

questions.prompt: If you see Tom, ___ him I have his ball.
questions.explain: The main clause can be an imperative: base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence giving advice is correct?
choices: If you are tired, you should to rest.
If you are tired, you should rest.
If you are tired, you shoulds rest.
If you will be tired, you should rest.
questions.answer: If you are tired, you should rest.
questions.explain: Modals (should, can, may, must) are followed by the base verb, and after if we use the present.

questions.prompt: If it stops raining, we ___ play outside.
questions.explain: Modal can + base verb is possible in the main clause.

questions.prompt: If Tom runs fast, he ___ win the race, but it is not certain.
questions.explain: Might + base verb expresses a possibility.

questions.prompt: If you want to join the team, you ___ come to training on Friday. It is compulsory.
questions.explain: Must + base verb expresses obligation.

questions.prompt: If it ___ stop raining, we won't play.
questions.explain: Negative in the if-clause: present simple, doesn't + base verb.

questions.prompt: If you ___ eat breakfast, you will feel tired.
questions.explain: Negative present simple with you: don't + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If Tom ___ (not / to study), he will fail the test.
questions.explain: Negative present simple with he: doesn't + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If we ___ (not / to leave) now, we will miss the train.
questions.explain: Negative present simple with we: don't + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If they ___ (not / to score), they won't win.
questions.explain: Negative present simple with they: don't + base verb.

questions.prompt: What ___ you do if it rains tomorrow?
questions.explain: Question in type 1: What will + subject + base verb + if + present?

questions.prompt: Which question about a bus is correct?
choices: What will you do if you will miss the bus?
What do you will do if you miss the bus?
What will you do if you miss the bus?
What you will do if you miss the bus?
questions.answer: What will you do if you miss the bus?
questions.explain: Main clause: will + subject + base verb; if-clause: present simple.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: What will Beowulf do if Grendel ___ (to come) tonight?
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if; Grendel takes -s.

questions.prompt: 'Will you play if it rains?' 'Yes, I ___.'
questions.explain: A short answer repeats the auxiliary: Yes, I will.

questions.prompt: If Grendel comes, ___ the doors!
questions.explain: The main clause can be an imperative.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If the sun ___ (to shine), we may go to the beach.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if, even with may in the main clause.

questions.prompt: We ___ the museum if we have time tomorrow.
questions.explain: Type 1 main clause: will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: I ___ (to be) angry if you lose my pen.
questions.explain: Type 1 main clause: will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (to get) 10 euros for my birthday, I will buy a football.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: If Beowulf wins, the king ___ him a reward.
questions.explain: Type 1 main clause: will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Hrothgar's men will celebrate if Beowulf ___ Grendel.
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: If you don't wear your boots, your feet ___ wet.
questions.explain: Type 1 main clause: will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about asking for help is correct?
choices: If you ask her, she will helps you.
If you ask her, she will help you.
If you ask her, she helps will you.
If you ask her, she will to help you.
questions.answer: If you ask her, she will help you.
questions.explain: After will, use the base verb with no -s.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about a message for a hero is correct?
choices: If I will see Beowulf, I will give him this message.
If I see Beowulf, I will give him this message.
If I would see Beowulf, I will give him this message.
If I saw Beowulf, I will give him this message.
questions.answer: If I see Beowulf, I will give him this message.
questions.explain: Type 1: if + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.explain: Unless = if ... not: present simple after unless, will in the main clause.

questions.prompt: 'We won't go out unless it stops raining.' means:
choices: We will go out if it keeps raining.
We will go out when it rains.
We will go out whatever the weather.
We will go out only if it stops raining.
questions.answer: We will go out only if it stops raining.
questions.explain: Unless = if ... not: we go out only if the rain stops.

questions.prompt: Which sentence with unless is correct?
choices: Unless you don't study, you will fail.
Unless you will study, you will fail.
Unless you study, you will fail.
Unless you studied, you will fail.
questions.answer: Unless you study, you will fail.
questions.explain: Unless already has a negative meaning: do not add not, and no will after it.

questions.prompt: Complete with one word: 'If you don't train, you won't improve.' = You won't improve ___ you train.
questions.explain: Unless = if ... not.

questions.prompt: Complete with one or two words: We will play outside unless it rains. = We will play outside if it ___ rain.
questions.explain: Unless it rains = if it doesn't rain.

questions.prompt: You can borrow my bike ___ you bring it back before dark.
questions.explain: As long as = only if (a condition).

questions.prompt: We will play tomorrow ___ the pitch is dry. If it is not, we will not play.
questions.explain: Provided that = only if.

questions.prompt: Take an umbrella ___ it rains later.
questions.explain: In case = as a precaution, because it might happen.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means you take a coat as a precaution, before it gets cold?
choices: I'll take a coat unless it gets cold.
I'll take a coat provided it gets cold.
I'll take a coat in case it gets cold.
I'll take a coat in case it will get cold.
questions.answer: I'll take a coat in case it gets cold.
questions.explain: In case + present simple expresses a precaution; no will after in case.

questions.prompt: Pack your boots ___ the pitch is muddy. (in case / unless / although)
questions.explain: In case = as a precaution, because it might happen.

questions.prompt: Beowulf will fight Grendel ___ the king gives him permission.
questions.explain: Provided that = only if.

questions.prompt: Unless the keeper is injured, he ___ in goal on Sunday.
questions.explain: Unless + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: Unless it ___ (to snow), the match will go ahead.
questions.explain: Unless + present simple; it takes -s.

questions.prompt: If I ___ you, I would talk to the coach.
questions.explain: Advice: If I were you, I would...

questions.prompt: If I had a lot of money, I ___ a big house.
questions.explain: Type 2 main clause: would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about winning a cup is correct?
choices: If I would win the cup, I would be happy.
If I won the cup, I would be happy.
If I will win the cup, I would be happy.
If I would have won the cup, I would be happy.
questions.answer: If I won the cup, I would be happy.
questions.explain: Type 2: if + past simple, would + base verb; never would after if.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about a swimming pool is correct?
choices: If we had a pool, we would swim every day.
If we would have a pool, we would swim every day.
If we will have a pool, we would swim every day.
If we had a pool, we will swim every day.
questions.answer: If we had a pool, we would swim every day.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple in the if-clause, would in the main clause.

questions.prompt: If Grendel ___ a friend, he wouldn't be so angry.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: If I had a bike, I ___ cycle to school.
questions.explain: Could + base verb is possible in a type 2 main clause.

questions.prompt: If I won a free trip, I ___ go to Japan, but I am not sure.
questions.explain: Might + base verb expresses a possibility in type 2.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (to be) a famous footballer, I would sign shirts every day.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if; were (or was) with I.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (to have) a time machine, I would visit the Vikings.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If Tom ___ (to know) the answer, he would tell us.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: She would buy a new phone if she ___ (to have) enough money.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If we ___ (to live) near the sea, we would go swimming every day.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (not / to be) so tired, I would play with you.
questions.explain: Type 2 negative: weren't (or wasn't) with I.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If they ___ (to train) more, they would win more games.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I were the coach, I ___ (to change) the tactics.
questions.explain: Type 2 main clause: would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If Beowulf ___ (to be) afraid of monsters, he wouldn't fight them.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if; were (or was).

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If the king ___ (to have) a bigger hall, he would invite more guests.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: I would travel the world if I ___ (to be) rich.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if; were (or was) with I.

questions.prompt: What would you do if you ___ invisible?
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple after if; were is the standard form.

questions.prompt: Which question about money is correct?
choices: What would you buy if you had £100?
What will you buy if you had £100?
What would you buy if you would have £100?
What you would buy if you had £100?
questions.answer: What would you buy if you had £100?
questions.explain: Type 2 question: would + subject + base verb, if + past simple.

questions.prompt: 'Would you go to the moon if you could?' 'Yes, I ___.'
questions.explain: A short answer repeats would: Yes, I would.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: If I ___ (not / to have) any homework, I would play football all afternoon.
questions.explain: Type 2 negative: didn't + base verb.

questions.prompt: If I were Beowulf, I ___ afraid of Grendel.
questions.explain: Type 2 negative main clause: wouldn't + base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence giving a warning is correct?
choices: If I would be you, I wouldn't do that.
If I were you, I wouldn't do that.
If I am you, I wouldn't do that.
If I was you, I won't do that.
questions.answer: If I were you, I wouldn't do that.
questions.explain: Type 2: if + past simple, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: If I would have a car, I would drive to work.
If I had wings, I would fly to school.
If I had a ticket, I would go to the final.
If we lived closer, we could meet more often.
questions.answer: If I would have a car, I would drive to work.
questions.explain: Never use would after if: If I had a car, I would drive to work.

questions.prompt: If I could fly, I ___ to Norway to see the home of the Vikings.
questions.explain: Type 2: past simple (could) in the if-clause, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: I do not speak Old English, but if I ___ speak it, I could read Beowulf in the original.
questions.explain: Type 2: could (past form of can) after if.

questions.prompt: Beowulf lived long ago. If he ___ here today, he would help our team.
questions.explain: Type 2: an imaginary situation (Beowulf is not here), so past simple after if.

questions.prompt: We are the favourites in tomorrow's final and we expect to win. Which sentence fits?
choices: If we won, we would get the cup.
If we win, we will get the cup.
If we will win, we will get the cup.
If we would win, we would get the cup.
questions.answer: If we win, we will get the cup.
questions.explain: We expect to win tomorrow, so winning is probable: type 1.

questions.prompt: Tom is 12, so he can't drive. Which sentence fits?
choices: If Tom were 18, he would drive to the stadium.
If Tom is 18, he will drive to the stadium.
If Tom were 18, he will drive to the stadium.
If Tom would be 18, he would drive to the stadium.
questions.answer: If Tom were 18, he would drive to the stadium.
questions.explain: Tom is 12, so being 18 is imaginary: type 2.

questions.prompt: I never buy lottery tickets, but if I ___ the lottery, I would travel the world.
questions.explain: Imaginary situation: type 2, past simple after if.

questions.prompt: Put the verb in the correct form: The forecast says it will be sunny tomorrow. If it ___ (to be) sunny, we will have a barbecue.
questions.explain: A probable situation: type 1, present simple after if.

questions.prompt: Mia says: 'If I ___ my room tomorrow, I can go to the match.'
questions.explain: A real possibility for tomorrow: type 1, present simple after if.

questions.prompt: Sam lives in a flat with no garden. If he ___ a garden, he would play football there.
questions.explain: He has no garden: imaginary, type 2.

questions.prompt: The keeper is ill and cannot play today. If he ___ fit, he would be in goal.
questions.explain: He is not fit: imaginary, type 2.

questions.prompt: Beowulf is on his way to Heorot. If he ___ tonight, Hrothgar will be happy.
questions.explain: His arrival is probable: type 1, present simple after if.

questions.prompt: Grendel is a monster and cannot talk. If Grendel ___ talk, he would explain his anger.
questions.explain: Grendel cannot talk: imaginary, type 2, so could after if.

questions.prompt: 'If I had a spaceship, I would visit Mars.' What does this sentence express?
questions.explain: If + past simple, would + base verb = imaginary (type 2).

questions.prompt: 'If I were a bird, I would fly south.' Is this situation real or imaginary? (real / imaginary)
questions.explain: If + past simple, would + base verb = imaginary.

questions.prompt: 'If you boil water, it turns into steam.' What does this sentence express? (general truth / future / imaginary)
questions.explain: Present simple in both clauses = general truth (type 0).

questions.prompt: Which sentence is about a probable future situation?
choices: If it snows tonight, we will go sledding.
If I had snow every day, I would go sledding every day.
If you heat snow, it melts.
If I were a snowman, I would hate the sun.
questions.answer: If it snows tonight, we will go sledding.
questions.explain: If + present simple, will + base verb = probable future.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is about an imaginary situation?
choices: If you press this button, the door opens.
If it rains, I'll take my umbrella.
If we win, we will celebrate.
If I were the referee, I would give a red card.
questions.answer: If I were the referee, I would give a red card.
questions.explain: If + past simple, would + base verb = imaginary.

questions.prompt: Which sentence talks about a general truth?
choices: If I find some paint tomorrow, I will paint my room.
If I mixed red and white, I would paint a pink wall.
If you will mix red and white, you get pink.
If you mix red and white, you get pink.
questions.answer: If you mix red and white, you get pink.
questions.explain: Present simple in both clauses = general truth.

questions.prompt: Choose the best ending: 'If it rains tomorrow, ...'
questions.explain: Type 1: if + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the best ending: 'If I had a magic wand, ...'
questions.explain: Type 2: if + past simple, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the best ending: 'If you heat chocolate, ...'
questions.explain: Type 0: present simple in both clauses.

questions.prompt: Choose the best ending: 'Unless you hurry, ...'
questions.explain: Unless + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the best ending: 'If Beowulf were here, ...'
questions.explain: Type 2: if + were, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the best beginning: '... we will go to the beach.'
choices: If the weather will be nice,
If the weather would be nice,
questions.explain: Type 1: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: Choose the best ending: 'I would help you if ...'
questions.explain: Type 2: if + past simple.
